eligibility.quote: The `sequence` node in the V3 behavior tree library works differently than in V2. There seems to be no way to have two subtrees running simultaneously in V3 unless you use the `parallel` node.
eligibility.reason: E1/E4: #1307 reproduces missing replanning and the fix author identifies the library-behavior change. E2: the separately built BT library and navigation consumer disagree about tick semantics; this is not merely a build or deployment fix. E3: UPGRADE is supported by the V2-to-V3 change and retained consumer expectations, even though the consumer was rebuilt for V3.

failed_conditions.quote: The Sequence node never ticks the CP subtree again because it is waiting for the FP subtree to complete and return a SUCCESS.
failed_conditions.reason: The demonstrated incompatibility is behavioral: whether completed children are re-ticked while a later child is RUNNING. It is not evidence that the consumed Sequence element has a different type/signature. Both inspected headers retain SequenceNode(const std::string& name) and BT::NodeStatus tick(); added implementation state/halt support does not make this observed failure a retyping. S1 has no dedicated semantic-protocol-change class, so use other. The implicated SequenceNode API is correct.

supporting_evidence.quote: * If any child returns RUNNING, previous children will be ticked again.
* If any child returns RUNNING, previous children will NOT be ticked again.

loudness.quote: I put print statements to see if the path was being calculated at 1Hz, and it was not. It was only being calculated once.
loudness.reason: The reporter discovers the failed behavioral expectation through instrumentation, not a build/connection/activation compatibility diagnostic.

detection_stage.quote: Obstacle appears in the global costmap, but the path is not updated.
detection_stage.reason: The failure is observed during navigation after an obstacle is placed in the current path.

resolution.quote: This uses an alternate control node that I'm calling PipelineSequence for lack of a better name.
resolution.reason: The merged alternative supplies a semantic fix; its general TB3/Gazebo test declaration does not identify both revisions of a successful reproduction of #1307. recommended is appropriate.

notes: The missed 1-Hz planning requests are evidence of this library/consumer semantic condition, not an additional rate_shortfall on a nonexistent rate port of SequenceNode. The planner-server composition and goal-preemption scenario are distinct. Exact BehaviorTree.CPP deployment revisions remain inferred from the specification; the directly inspected 2.5.2 and 3.0.9 declarations establish the semantic contrast without establishing the reporter's exact library binary.
